title: Introduction to Relational Databases
text: A relational database organises data into tables with rows and columns. Relationships between tables are expressed through foreign keys and enforced by the database engine. SQL (Structured Query Language) is the standard language for querying relational databases and supports joins, aggregations, transactions, and complex filtering. PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQLite are popular open-source relational databases.

title: NoSQL Document Databases
text: Document databases store data as semi-structured documents — typically JSON or BSON — rather than normalised rows and columns. Each document can have a flexible schema, making them well-suited to hierarchical or polymorphic data. MongoDB is the most widely deployed document database and supports rich query expressions, secondary indexes, aggregation pipelines, and horizontal sharding.

title: Vector Databases and Approximate Nearest Neighbour Search
text: Vector databases store high-dimensional embeddings and support approximate nearest-neighbour (ANN) search. They are the backbone of modern semantic search and recommendation systems. Qdrant is an open-source vector database that supports HNSW indexing, payload filtering, and real-time updates. Other options include Pinecone, Weaviate, and Milvus.

title: Supervised Machine Learning
text: Supervised learning trains a model on labelled examples (input-output pairs) so that it can generalise to new, unseen inputs. Common algorithms include linear regression, logistic regression, decision trees, random forests, gradient boosted trees (XGBoost, LightGBM), and neural networks. Model selection is guided by cross-validation and holdout evaluation on a test split.

title: Transformer Architecture and Large Language Models
text: The Transformer architecture introduced by Vaswani et al. in 2017 replaced recurrence with self-attention, enabling massively parallel training on long sequences. Pre-trained large language models (LLMs) such as GPT-4, Claude, and LLaMA learn rich representations of language by predicting next tokens over vast text corpora. Fine-tuning or retrieval augmentation adapts them to downstream tasks.

title: Algorithmic Trading and Market Microstructure
text: Algorithmic trading uses computer programs to execute orders according to pre-defined rules, capturing short-lived price discrepancies or responding to market signals faster than human traders. Market microstructure studies the process by which securities prices are determined, including the role of order books, bid-ask spreads, latency arbitrage, and market makers.

title: Risk Management in Financial Systems
text: Financial risk management identifies, quantifies, and mitigates exposures arising from market movements, credit defaults, operational failures, and liquidity crises. Key frameworks include Value-at-Risk (VaR), Expected Shortfall, stress testing, and scenario analysis. Regulatory requirements such as Basel III impose minimum capital ratios on banks to absorb unexpected losses.

title: TCP/IP and the Internet Protocol Suite
text: The TCP/IP model layers network communication into four abstractions: network access, internet, transport, and application. IP provides best-effort packet routing across heterogeneous networks. TCP adds reliable, ordered delivery through sequence numbers and acknowledgements. UDP sacrifices reliability for lower overhead, favoured by video streaming and DNS.

title: Content Delivery Networks and Edge Computing
text: A Content Delivery Network (CDN) distributes static and dynamic content across geographically distributed edge nodes, reducing round-trip latency for end users. Cloudflare, Fastly, and Amazon CloudFront are major CDN providers. Edge computing extends this concept by running compute workloads at or near the edge, reducing the need to transmit raw data to centralised data centres.

title: Linux Kernel and Process Scheduling
text: The Linux kernel is a monolithic, modular kernel that manages hardware abstraction, memory, processes, file systems, and networking. The Completely Fair Scheduler (CFS) allocates CPU time proportionally using a red-black tree keyed on virtual run time. Real-time scheduling classes (SCHED_FIFO, SCHED_RR) are available for latency-sensitive workloads.

title: Memory Management and Virtual Memory
text: Virtual memory decouples a process's address space from physical RAM, enabling memory isolation, demand paging, and overcommit. The operating system maintains page tables mapping virtual addresses to physical frames. Page faults trigger on-demand loading from disk. Memory-mapped files, copy-on-write, and huge pages are important optimisations.

title: ACID Transactions and Isolation Levels
text: ACID stands for Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability. These properties guarantee that database transactions are processed reliably even in the presence of failures. Isolation levels (Read Uncommitted, Read Committed, Repeatable Read, Serializable) trade correctness for concurrency. PostgreSQL implements multi-version concurrency control (MVCC) to achieve high read throughput without locking.
